# The relation-level reading's law of easing, and restraint under it

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`relation-level-law-of-easing` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](relation-level-law-of-easing.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Read relation by relation, easing withdraws exactly the relations the easing course no longer takes part in or undermines; restraint that lets no level fall and keeps taking part ranks above overdraw for any number of drawers under the relation-level reading too.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. The relation-level reading on courses: a claim is a formation's relation to a condition at a step, included when the formation is active, takes part in the condition and the relation does not undermine; it is the living of Web.relations. (`Becoming.Ranking.relational`, `Becoming.Ranking.relational_iff`)
2. The relation-level law of easing: under easing a relation the reading includes in the first course stays included in the second exactly where the second still takes part and does not undermine there, so the second extends the first exactly when it takes part in and does not undermine every relation the first includes and includes one it withholds. (`Becoming.Ranking.relational_kept_iff`, `Becoming.Ranking.relational_extends_iff_of_eases`)
3. Where no level falls in the easing course and it takes part wherever the other does, it extends the other under the relation-level reading exactly when it includes a relation the other withholds. (`Becoming.Ranking.relational_extends_iff_of_rising`)
4. In the two-part family the relation-level reading includes the focal formation's relation where the stepwise reading includes its event, so absence and occurrence are unranked, as under the stepwise reading. (`Becoming.Ranking.relational_unranked`)
5. Restraint over any number of drawers under the relation-level reading: under the stepwise restraint theorem's premises, where the restrained course also takes part in every condition wherever the other does, it extends the other exactly when it includes a relation the other withholds. (`Becoming.Ranking.restraint_extends_iff_relational`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom. The readings of living (relation-level: a formation's relation to a condition, active, taking part and not undermining); each law's own premises as hypotheses: the gating of activity, easing; for restraint, balanced flows, the restrained flow taking no more, giving no less and within what it gives, and taking part wherever the other does.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- That participation kept is needed beyond each relation the other includes: the exact law asks it relation by relation.
- Restraint by abstaining: a course that stops drawing on and depending on a condition loses its relations to it, so this law does not rank it.
- Which reading of living to use; the form of L under the condition; J1 step by step.

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · A law of the formal model; its correspondence to actual systems is a separate obligation. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · A relation omitted by a weaker description does not refute the fuller account.

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

The comparison laws are the theory's own. The three readings of living now each have an exact law of easing: the whole-run law needs easing and the gating of activity; the stepwise law adds that the easing course undermine no included event; the relation-level law adds that it keep taking part in every included relation.
